## Implemented architecture

The workflow integrates HyP3/MintPy ascending and descending series, tropospheric correction, spatial referencing, LOS products, temporal pairing, east–vertical decomposition under dN=0, AOI and elevation-band statistics, atlases and trend tables.

<div class="ma-data-strip"><div><strong>33</strong><span>ascending acquisitions</span></div><div><strong>35</strong><span>descending acquisitions</span></div><div><strong>40 m</strong><span>common resolution</span></div><div><strong>−0.95</strong><span>approximate determinant</span></div></div>

## Signal and detection capability

<figure class="ma-science-figure"><img src="/assets/img/charts/insar-noise-en.svg" alt="Monthly relative vertical displacement medians compared with the stable-terrain InSAR residual" width="1000" height="470" loading="lazy"><figcaption>Audited examples: +0.23 cm in December 2023 and −0.58 cm in January 2024; stable residual 0.63–0.65 cm.</figcaption></figure>

Monthly vertical signals lie within or close to the noise floor. The publishable contribution must focus on cumulative products, elevation profiles, quality, uncertainty and multi-sensor comparison. A final regional dU rate is not yet reported.

## Physical restriction

dU is relative vertical motion of coherent scatterers under dN=0. It is not Eulerian elevation change or mass balance. Comparison with ICESat‑2 requires common windows, rates/cumulative displacement and coherent slow-flow zones.
